subtitle: Journal-club style ICU update: PICO, key results, appraisal, bedside impact, and medical English.

script.heading: Intro
sentences: Welcome to Critical Care Daily for November 03, 2026.
Today we will review 3 recent ICU-relevant publications.
The format is quick listen first, then PICO, key results, critical appraisal, bedside impact, and medical English notes.
Use this as a morning triage tool, then open the source link for full-text appraisal before changing practice.

script.heading: Story 1 - Sodium bicarbonate therapy for metabolic acidosis in criticall
sentences: Story 1 is about Sodium bicarbonate therapy for metabolic acidosis in critically ill patients: a Bayesian systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials..
This is a systematic review / meta-analysis from Intensive care medicine.

The clinical question is best framed as follows: in adult intensive care unit patients with metabolic acidosis, how should we interpret Exposure or intervention stated in the title/objective. compared with Comparator or control group stated in the methods/results, if present.?
Four RCTs including 1544 patients were analysed.
Sodium bicarbonate did not show a clear short-term mortality benefit (RR 0.94, 95% CrI 0.73-1.22), with a posterior probability of benefit of 72.1%.
For RRT initiation, sodium bicarbonate was associated with a lower risk (RR 0.74, 95% CrI 0.59-0.98), with a posterior probability of benefit of 97.2%.
For critical appraisal, focus on whether the design supports a causal conclusion and whether the patients resemble your ICU population.
The bedside implication is this: Do not change practice on efficacy alone; focus journal-club discussion on whether the confidence intervals exclude a clinically important benefit or harm.
Useful English phrase: these findings should be interpreted cautiously because the details of design and applicability matter.

script.heading: Story 2 - Individualized treatment effects of high flow nasal oxygen in
sentences: Story 2 is about Individualized treatment effects of high flow nasal oxygen in immunocompromised patients..
This is a recent research article from Intensive care medicine.

The clinical question is best framed as follows: in patients randomized to HFNO or conventional oxygen) to predict the HFNO effects on day-28 IMV incidence, how should we interpret Exposure or intervention stated in the title/objective. compared with Comparator or control group stated in the methods/results, if present.?
Among the 704 participants, HFNO's average effect on day-28 IMV was not significant.

However, substantial heterogeneity in treatment responses was identified (predicted benefit: from 20.2% [IQR 15.5%-23.9%] absolute IMV risk reduction with HFNO to 7.4% risk reduction [2.9%-11.2%] with conventional oxygen).

Patients with the highest predicted benefit were older, more frequently solid organ transplant recipients, less neutropenic, more severely hypoxemic/tachycardic, but with lower non-respiratory sequential organ failure assessment (SOFA) scores.
For critical appraisal, focus on whether the design supports a causal conclusion and whether the patients resemble your ICU population.

script.heading: Story 3 - Functional Connectivity at Birth and Longitudinal Neurocogniti
sentences: Story 3 is about Functional Connectivity at Birth and Longitudinal Neurocognitive Development in Very Preterm Infants..
This is a recent research article from JAMA network open.

The clinical question is best framed as follows: in intensive care units in the greater Cincinnati, Ohio, area between September 16, 2016, and November 19, 2019, how should we interpret Exposure or intervention stated in the title/objective. compared with Comparator or control group stated in the methods/results, if present.?
A total of 257 infants born VPT (mean [SD] gestational age, 29.2 [2.5] weeks; 132 male [51.4%]) were included in the final longitudinal analysis.

Stronger neonatal connectivity involving the DMN was positively associated with cognitive performance, including intra-DMN (0.23; 95% credible interval [CrI], 0.06-0.39) and DMN connections with the frontoparietal control network (0.24; 95% CrI, 0.07-0.40), SMN (0.20; 95% CrI, 0.02-0.37), VIS (0.32; 95% CrI, 0.13-0.51), and CO (0.39; 95% CrI, 0.21-0.56).
Positive associations were also observed for SMN-VIS (0.27; 95% CrI, 0.12-0.43) and SMN-CO (0.26; 95% CrI, 0.09-0.44) connectivity.
For critical appraisal, focus on whether the design supports a causal conclusion and whether the patients resemble your ICU population.
The bedside implication is this: Use as an awareness item; read the full article before applying it clinically.
Useful English phrase: these findings should be interpreted cautiously because the details of design and applicability matter.

script.heading: Outro
sentences: That wraps up today's journal club style update.
Before applying any finding, check the full source, the absolute effect size, and your local ICU context.
For English practice, repeat one academic phrase from each article out loud.

articles.title: Sodium bicarbonate therapy for metabolic acidosis in critically ill patients: a Bayesian systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
articles.summary: We performed a systematic review and Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials (RCTs) comparing intravenous sodium bicarbonate with placebo or usual care in adult intensive care unit patients with metabolic acidosis. Four RCTs including 1544 patients were analysed. Sodium bicarbonate did not show a clear short-term mortality benefit (RR 0.94, 95% CrI 0.73-1.22), with a posterior probability of benefit of 72.1%. For RRT initiation, sodium bicarbonate was associated with a lower risk (RR 0.74, 95% CrI 0.59-0.98), with a posterior probability of benefit of 97.2%. Effects on other outcomes were small or imprecise, and no consistent safety signal was identified.

articles.title: Individualized treatment effects of high flow nasal oxygen in immunocompromised patients.
articles.summary: A causal forest machine-learning algorithm was derived in the HIGH trial (776 patients randomized to HFNO or conventional oxygen) to predict the HFNO effects on day-28 IMV incidence. Transportability of the model was assessed in an independent observational cohort (818 patients). Among the 704 participants, HFNO's average effect on day-28 IMV was not significant. However, substantial heterogeneity in treatment responses was identified (predicted benefit: from 20.2% [IQR 15.5%-23.9%] absolute IMV risk reduction with HFNO to 7.4% risk reduction [2.9%-11.2%] with conventional oxygen). High flow nasal oxygen (HFNO) has become a common first-line practice for acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (ARF).

articles.title: Functional Connectivity at Birth and Longitudinal Neurocognitive Development in Very Preterm Infants.
articles.summary: A total of 257 infants born VPT (mean [SD] gestational age, 29.2 [2.5] weeks; 132 male [51.4%]) were included in the final longitudinal analysis. Stronger neonatal connectivity involving the DMN was positively associated with cognitive performance, including intra-DMN (0.23; 95% credible interval [CrI], 0.06-0.39) and DMN connections with the frontoparietal control network (0.24; 95% CrI, 0.07-0.40), SMN (0.20; 95% CrI, 0.02-0.37), VIS (0.32; 95% CrI, 0.13-0.51), and CO (0.39; 95% CrI, 0.21-0.56). Positive associations were also observed for SMN-VIS (0.27; 95% CrI, 0.12-0.43) and SMN-CO (0.26; 95% CrI, 0.09-0.44) connectivity. The SMN-VIS was the only connection showing a difference between assessments, with a less pronounced association at 3 years than at 2 years (interaction, -0.09; 95% CrI, -0.20 to <0.01). Understanding how neonatal functional connectivity at birth is associated with later cognitive performance in infants born very preterm (VPT) may help identify early neuroimaging markers of neurodevelopment.
